Honestly, I don't think there's any good way to "challenge" her beliefs. I think your best bet is to simply ask her about her beliefs and ask her to explain the things you don't understand about the belief. At some point you'll inevitably hit an indoctrination wall where "I don't know" is the only answer she can give. Exploring her beliefs will either lead her question them and perhaps forgo them, or it will lead to the "I don't know" and be unable to progress.

Directly challenging the belief or pointing out conundrums or fallacies or contradictions is probably just going to throw her into a defensive position where she will double down, and the discussion will dissolve into something unproductive, if not damaging. Asking someone to answer for, and speak on behalf of, the entire religion puts them into an impossible situation. It'd be like someone demanding you prove the universe is expanding, or that quantum physics is about probability. Your answer would essentially be "because these people say that's how it is" even if the evidence is demonstrable, in those cases. You can't change someone's faith, you can only guide them towards a place where they will change what they believe.

My advice would be to just talk to her about it, make your doubts clear but don't be aggressive, respect her beliefs with the understanding that she will respect yours (which I presume is believing there are no gods.)
